source_title: Amana ZrN-Coated and Uncoated 2D/3D Carving CNC Solid Carbide Router Bits chip load chart (v8)
coverage_notes: Current version of the chart the LUT cites as amana_zrn_3d_profiling_v8 (the manifest entry has no stored text or hash). One 'Wood, MDF, Sign-Foam' row per section; header 'Operating RPM: 18,000 / Depth of Cut: 1 x Tool Diameter'. The chart keys the chip load on the tool 'Dia.'; the tool numbers in each section are identified in amana_46xxx_identity: most ball tools here are TAPERED ball carving bits keyed on the tip. Tapered cells printed: 2 flute at 1 mm, 1/16", 1/4" (46256, 46252, 46283); 3 flute at 1/32"-1mm, 1/8"-3.2mm, 3/16" (46280/46291/46580/46470, 46284/46286/46287/46288/46474, 46298); 4 flute at 1.5 mm, 1/16", 1/8" (46472, 46282/46293/46582, 46583; the 4 flute value is the same at every size). Differences from v1: v8 adds 46473 (0.5 mm tip) to the 3 flute list with no 0.5 mm column; v8 fixes the v1 3 flute extra-long typo 0.0004" - 0.006" to 0.004" - 0.006"; v8 adds a 3/16"-1/4" and a 3/8" column to the 3 flute flat bottom; v8 says 'Reduce feed rate' where v1 says 'Reduce chip load'. Self-inconsistent cells (printed IPM vs chip load): 2 flute 1/16" (IPM gives half), 3 flute 1/8"-3.2mm top, 3/16". 27 candidate rows (9 cells x softwood/hardwood/MDF).

source_title: Amana 46xxx carving bits: product spec per tool number listed on the ZrN 2D/3D carving chart
source_url: https://fastoolnow.com/search.php?search_query=<tool number> (one product page per number; each URL and raw-page sha256 is in the stored text)
coverage_notes: Built by scripts/g1_amana_identity.py. amanatool.com returns a Cloudflare challenge to curl, so the spec blocks come from distributor product pages (fastoolnow first, toolstoday or arrowtooling where the search is empty). Identified: 34 of 39 unique numbers (corrected by the reconciler; see below). Not identified: 46285, 46289, 46496, 46593, 46596. Key facts: 46256 = 5.4 deg taper, 1mm D x 0.5mm R, 2 flutes; 46471 = 0.10 deg (straight) 1mm ball; 46280/46291/46580 = 6.2 deg taper 1/32" D, 3 flutes; 46470 = 6.2 deg 0.8 D; 46473 = 6.2 deg 0.5 D; 46472 = 5.4 deg 1.5 D 4 flutes. The hash is of the stored text (HTML sources). Reconciler 2026-09-24 (verifier findings): the stored text has 40 blocks for 39 unique numbers (46471 twice); 34 of 39 are identified, not '36 of 41'; the v8 chart prints 54 distinct 46xxx numbers and the flat-bottom 4657x series is not covered. The 46280 page prints only 'Tapered ... 1/32" D'; its 6.2 deg and 3 flutes are DERIVED from the chart section and the siblings 46291/46580. The stored titles of 46470 and 46472 are cut before 'Flute'; their flute counts read from the live page body only.

source_title: SpeTool WOODWORKING 2D/3D ROUTER BIT FEED&SPEED CHART
coverage_notes: One-page scanned chart (OCR layer; the stored text has a transcription from the page image plus the raw OCR). Keyed on 'Tip Diameter' at 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0 mm and 1/32, 1/16, 1/8 in: 9 sizes, one chip load each (no band), one 'Wood, MDF, Sign-Foam' row, 18,000 RPM, depth of cut 1 x cutting diameter, step down = 1 x tip, step over = 0.4 x tip. No unit and no flute count printed: feed / (RPM x chipload) = 2.00 on all 9 wood rows, so inch per tooth and 2 flutes are derived. Tapered identity from the file name and the index page (spetool_speed_feeds_index). The only printed 0.5 mm wood figure found. 27 candidate rows (9 sizes x softwood/hardwood/MDF).

source_title: SpeTool WOODWORKING CARBIDE SPIRAL ROUTER BIT FEED&SPEED CHART
coverage_notes: Scanned chart, flat spiral bits 1/16, 1/8, 1/4, 3/8, 1/2 in; MDF Laminate, softwood and hardwood printed apart; up, down and compression (compression from 1/8 in). One value per cell, no band. Flute count derived as 2 from the feed identity (range 1.94-2.13; the chart rounds its feeds). Smallest size 1/16 in, so no sub-1.5 mm row. 42 candidate rows. Also useful to G2 (hardwood/softwood/MDF ratios) and G4 (no band).

source_title: SpeTool WOODWORKING V-GROOVE & SIGNMAKING ROUTER BIT FEED&SPEED CHART
coverage_notes: Engraving tips 0.005 and 0.015 in print the SAME chip load per material (hardwood 0.003, softwood 0.005, MDF 0.007); the V-bit rows print no size. Not a size series; no candidate rows. Recorded as a witness that this vendor does not scale engraving chip load with tip width.

source_title: PreciseBits: Finding the Sweet Spot When Machining with Carbide Microtools
coverage_notes: No chart. Prints a starting rule for a feed test: 'Softwoods ... Hardwoods ... Extreme hardwoods: F = 0.03 x D x No. flutes x RPM (3% chipload per flute)', 'just below the sweetspot', then raise the feed until the cut fails and use 0.75 x Fmax. A D^1.0 start rule, the same for every wood hardness. Not a recommendation value; no candidate rows. Hash of the stored text.

coverage_notes: 13 tools 77-102 to 77-116(M): 77-102..77-108 '3 flute', 77-112..77-116 '2 flute'. Confirms the LUT flute counts. The Onsrud wood sheets print 77-100 at 1/8 and 1/4 in only; no smaller 77-100 tip exists in the series. No rows.
